newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen up sharply on BOJ tankan rumours.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen up sharply on BOJ tankan rumours.

text.p: The key March Euroyen contract rose sharply by mid-morning Tokyo on various market rumours about possible weakness in the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) quarterly corporate sentiment survey due on Wednesday, traders said.
The March was at 98.94, up sharply from Monday's 98.87.
There was widespread talk that a senior BOJ official implied in a meeting with some Japanese bank managers on Monday that the tankan would show weak results.
The Euroyen was also bought on talk that a major U.S. brokerage firm which had a relatively optimistic forecast for the tankan was revising it down, traders said.
In the IRS market, there was speculation that a long-term bank received a large amount of seven-year fixed interest rates.
The seven-year IRS was quoted at 2.42/2.46 percent, down sharply from Monday's 2.47/2.51 percent.
Tokyo traders said that on SIMEX, a U.S. speculative fund bought the March contract in a large lot in early trading.
